**Scope**: 2 C# projects, 2 F# projects, 2 `Directory.Build.props`, 2 `Directory.Build.targets`, 1 solution file.

## 🔴 Errors (will cause build failures or silent misbehavior)

### 1. `Directory.Build.props` — `$(TargetFramework)` condition in `.props` is always false (AP-21)

**File**: `Directory.Build.props:10`
```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem**: For single-targeting projects (like LibA and LibB that set `<TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>`), `$(TargetFramework)` is **empty** during `.props` evaluation. The SDK's outer-build/inner-build dispatch hasn't set the value yet. This condition will **never** match, so `GenerateDocumentationFile` is silently never enabled for any project in the repo.

**Fix**: Move this conditional to `Directory.Build.targets`, where `$(TargetFramework)` is populated:
```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.targets -->
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 2. `Directory.Build.targets` — Property defaults in `.targets` silently override project-level settings

**File**: `Directory.Build.targets:6-10`
```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company>Contoso</Company>
  <Authors>Build Team</Authors>
  <Copyright>Copyright 2024 Contoso</Copyright>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem**: `.targets` is imported **after** the project file. This means `TreatWarningsAsErrors=true` unconditionally **overwrites** any value set in a `.csproj`. LibB explicitly sets `<TreatWarningsAsErrors>false</TreatWarningsAsErrors>` (line 13), but that setting is silently crushed by this file. The same applies to `Company`/`Authors`/`Copyright` — no project can override them.

**Fix**: Move these to `Directory.Build.props` as conditional defaults so projects can override them:
```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.props -->
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors Condition="'$(TreatWarningsAsErrors)' == ''">true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company Condition="'$(Company)' == ''">Contoso</Company>
  <Authors Condition="'$(Authors)' == ''">Build Team</Authors>
  <Copyright Condition="'$(Copyright)' == ''">Copyright 2024 Contoso</Copyright>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 3. `LibA.csproj:13` — Unquoted condition (AP-04)

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="$(Configuration) == Debug">
```

**Problem**: Both sides of the comparison are unquoted. If `$(Configuration)` is empty (e.g., during certain evaluation phases or IDE design-time builds), this expands to ` == Debug`, which is a **syntax error** (MSB4100). Even when it works, it's fragile if the value ever contains spaces.

**Fix**:
```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'">
```

---

### 4. `LibA.csproj:14` — `DefineConstants` overwrite destroys SDK defaults (AP-07)

```xml
<DefineConstants>ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

**Problem**: This **replaces** the entire `DefineConstants` value. The SDK default sets `TRACE` (and `DEBUG` in Debug configuration). After this line, all of those are gone. Any code using `#if TRACE` or `#if DEBUG` silently stops working.

**Fix**: Append instead of overwrite:
```xml
<DefineConstants>$(DefineConstants);ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

---

### 5. `LibA.csproj:7` & `LibB.csproj:7` — Hardcoded Windows-absolute `OutputPath` (AP-06)

```xml
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibA</OutputPath>
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibB</OutputPath>
```

**Problem**: These are absolute Windows paths. On Linux/macOS (CI agents, containers, dev machines), MSBuild will attempt to create `/C:/builds/output/LibA` or fail entirely. Even on Windows, this ties the build to a specific machine layout.

**Fix**: Use relative paths or a configurable property:
```xml
<OutputPath>$(RepoRoot)artifacts\bin\LibA\</OutputPath>
```
Or simply remove them and let the SDK default (`bin\$(Configuration)\$(TargetFramework)\`) work.

---

### 6. `fsharp/BrokenOrder/BrokenOrder.fsproj` — Wrong F# compile order

```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <Compile Include="Services.fs" />   <!-- depends on Domain -->
  <Compile Include="Domain.fs" />     <!-- defines the types -->
  <Compile Include="Program.fs" />
</ItemGroup>
```

**Problem**: F# compilation is **order-dependent**. `Services.fs` has `open BrokenOrder.Domain`, but `Domain.fs` (which defines that module) appears **after** it. The F# compiler processes files top-to-bottom, so this will produce a compile error: `The namespace or module 'BrokenOrder.Domain' is not defined`.

**Fix**: Put `Domain.fs` first:
```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
  <Compile Include="Services.fs" />
  <Compile Include="Program.fs" />
</ItemGroup>
```
*(Note: `fsharp/OrderService/OrderService.fsproj` has the correct order — this is only broken in `BrokenOrder`.)*

### 7. `LibA.csproj:27-29` — Legacy assembly `<Reference>` with HintPath to `packages\` folder (AP-02)

```xml
<Reference Include="Newtonsoft.Json">
  <HintPath>..\packages\Newtonsoft.Json.13.0.3\lib\net6.0\Newtonsoft.Json.dll</HintPath>
</Reference>
```

**Problem**: This is a `packages.config`-era pattern. It manually points to a NuGet package DLL on disk. There's no automatic restore, no transitive dependency resolution, and the `net6.0` TFM in the path doesn't match the project's `net8.0` target — so you're loading a potentially wrong TFM asset.

**Fix**: Replace with a `PackageReference`:
```xml
<PackageReference Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
```

### 8. `Directory.Build.props:17` — Analyzer package missing `PrivateAssets="all"`

<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556" />

**Fix**:

<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556">

  <IncludeAssets>runtime; build; native; contentfiles; analyzers</IncludeAssets>

### 9. `LibA.csproj:21-23` — Redundant `<Compile Include>` for SDK-globbed file + mixed Include/Update (AP-10)

<Compile Include="Class1.cs" />
<Compile Update="Class1.cs" AutoGen="true" />
